steps.name: Implement NaN-safe clampedValue on ProgressBar
steps.description: Replace the RED scaffold body of ProgressBar.clampedValue with the NaN-safe negated-comparison clamp specified in ADR-005 Decision 2, and delete the __SCAFFOLD__ marker. No other source file is touched.
criteria: clampedValue returns 1.0 for any value above 1.0, including positive infinity
clampedValue returns 0.0 for any value below 0.0, for negative infinity, and for NaN
clampedValue equals value exactly for inputs within 0.0...1.0, including both endpoints
clampedValue lies within 0.0...1.0 for every Float input and is identical on repeated reads
All 20 ProgressBar acceptance tests pass, full suite stays green, no __SCAFFOLD__ marker remains

files_to_modify.change: Replace the `.nan` scaffold body of `clampedValue` with the ADR-005 Decision 2 clamp, and delete the file-level `let __SCAFFOLD__ = true` marker (line 14) plus the RED-scaffold comment block referring to it.

steps.implementation_notes:
ADR-005 Decision 2 specifies the implementation exactly and it is normative, not stylistic:

    public var clampedValue: Float {
        if !(value > 0) { return 0 }   // negated comparison: NaN lands here
        if value > 1 { return 1 }
        return value
    }

DO NOT use `min`/`max`. Both propagate NaN, so `min(1, max(0, .nan))` returns NaN and AC-10 (`a NaN shield charge resolves to an empty bar rather than crashing or filling`) fails at exactly the input the guarantee exists for. The negated comparison `!(value > 0)` is NaN-safe because every comparison against NaN is false, so NaN falls into the zero branch.

DELETE `let __SCAFFOLD__ = true` from the top of Sources/GameUI/ProgressBar.swift. Verify with `grep -rn "__SCAFFOLD__" Sources/` — zero markers must remain after DELIVER (DISTILL Mandate 7).

Do NOT modify LayoutEngine.swift, HitTest.swift, Color.swift, View.swift, or Slider.swift. DDD-4/DDD-5 obtain layout and hit-test behaviour by reuse and the corresponding tests are already green; ADR-005 further constrains ProgressBar from ever conforming to AnyButton, ContainerView, ZStackView, HasFrameSize, or AnyDirectionalPaddingModifier — any such conformance silently redirects both layoutNode and hitTestNode and breaks AC-04/AC-06.

Constraints from CLAUDE.md: Swift 6.2, no `import Foundation`, `Float` geometry only, Swift Testing with backtick-quoted names, value types only. Note F-1 (open, repo-wide): this repo has no CI, so the no-Foundation constraint is enforced by code review only — check it by eye.

MUTATION TESTING: skipped per CLAUDE.md (Muter is not reliably available in this environment).

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM (Hypothesis form): this is a Swift package with no third-party dependencies permitted, so Hypothesis @given strategies and assert_state_delta do not exist here. The substance of the mandate is nonetheless satisfied by tests DISTILL already committed: AC-12 is covered as a property two ways — a curated 23-value special-float set (`0`, `±0`, `1`, `1±ulp`, `±∞`, `NaN`, `signalingNaN`, subnormals, `greatestFiniteMagnitude`) and a 4096-value seeded SplitMix64 sweep over raw Float bit patterns (fixed seeds 0xC0FFEE / 0x5EED, reproducible, reports first counterexample). The universe is trivially closed: ProgressBar is a frozen immutable struct with no driven ports, no I/O, and no mutable state, so there is no state delta to declare. `clampedValue` is a pure function of one stored property (Principle 12 contract shape: pure-function, return-only). Do NOT add new Hypothesis-shaped tests; do NOT modify any existing test file (DoD item 7).

Run: `swift test --disable-sandbox`. Expect 175 tests, 0 issues.
